entries.originalText: Blessed is he who understandeth what it is to love Jesus, and to despise himself for Jesus’ sake.
entries.modernizedText: Blessed is the person who understands what it is to love Jesus and to despise himself for Jesus’ sake.

entries.originalText: He must give up all that he loveth for his Beloved, for Jesus will be loved alone above all things.
entries.modernizedText: He must give up all that he loves for his Beloved, for Jesus will be loved alone above all things.

entries.originalText: The love of created things is deceiving and unstable, but the love of Jesus is faithful and lasting.
entries.modernizedText: The love of created things is deceptive and unstable, but the love of Jesus is faithful and lasting.

entries.originalText: He who cleaveth to created things will fall with their slipperiness; but he who embraceth Jesus will stand upright for ever.
entries.modernizedText: The person who clings to created things will fall with their slipperiness, but the person who embraces Jesus will stand upright forever.

entries.originalText: Love Him and hold Him for thy friend, for He will not forsake thee when all depart from thee, nor will he suffer thee to perish at the last.
entries.modernizedText: Love Him and hold Him as your friend, for He will not forsake you when all depart from you, nor will He allow you to perish at the end.

entries.originalText: Thou must one day be separated from all, whether thou wilt or wilt not.
entries.modernizedText: One day you must be separated from all, whether you will or not.

entries.originalText: Cleave thou to Jesus in life and death, and commit thyself unto His faithfulness, who, when all men fail thee, is alone able to help thee.
entries.modernizedText: Cling to Jesus in life and death, and commit yourself to His faithfulness, who alone is able to help you when all others fail you.

entries.originalText: Thy Beloved is such, by nature, that He will suffer no rival, but alone will possess thy heart, and as a king will sit upon His own throne.
entries.modernizedText: Your Beloved is such by nature that He will suffer no rival, but will possess your heart alone and sit as a king upon His own throne.

entries.originalText: If thou wouldst learn to put away from thee every created thing, Jesus would freely take up His abode with thee.
entries.modernizedText: If you would learn to put away every created thing, Jesus would freely take up His dwelling with you.

entries.originalText: Thou wilt find all trust little better than lost which thou hast placed in men, and not in Jesus.
entries.modernizedText: You will find all trust that you have placed in people and not in Jesus little better than lost.

entries.originalText: Trust not nor lean upon a reed shaken with the wind, because all flesh is grass, and the goodliness thereof falleth as the flower of the field.(1)
entries.modernizedText: Do not trust or lean upon a reed shaken by the wind, because all flesh is grass, and its beauty falls like the flower of the field.(1)

entries.originalText: Thou wilt be quickly deceived if thou lookest only upon the outward appearance of men, for if thou seekest thy comfort and profit in others, thou shalt too often experience loss.
entries.modernizedText: You will quickly be deceived if you look only at the outward appearance of people, for if you seek your comfort and benefit in others, you will too often experience loss.

entries.originalText: If thou seekest Jesus in all things thou shalt verily find Jesus, but if thou seekest thyself thou shalt also find thyself, but to thine own hurt.
entries.modernizedText: If you seek Jesus in all things you will truly find Jesus, but if you seek yourself you will also find yourself, but to your own hurt.

entries.originalText: For if a man seeketh not Jesus he is more hurtful to himself than all the world and all his adversaries.
entries.modernizedText: For if a person does not seek Jesus, he is more hurtful to himself than all the world and all his adversaries.
